issues.description: Glutamatergic identity is inherited from the BLA principal-neuron class; the new quote characterizes fear vs extinction populations functionally and does not state NT type explicitly.

No molecular marker is reported for the fear (Fear-On) population in the new PDF; only the extinction/Fear-Off population was molecularly resolved (Ntsr2/Dkk3/Rspo2/Wnt7a). Fear neuron remains functionally/circuit-defined.

basal_amygdala_fear_neuron.new_evidence_summary: Cardenas et al. 2019 establishes the fear neuron as one of two functionally distinct, non-overlapping BLA principal-cell populations: activated by the conditioned stimulus, projecting to mPFC. No molecular marker for the fear-specific population.

issues.description: Markers (Ntsr2, Dkk3, Rspo2, Wnt7a) derive from activity-guided RNA-seq of a Thy1-labeled 'Fear-Off' population in mouse; Ntsr2 is the validated handle. Equating the Thy1/Fear-Off molecular population with the Herry 'extinction' neuron is a cross-study inference, not a single-paper identity.
Glutamatergic identity inherited from BLA principal-neuron class; new quotes do not state NT type explicitly.

basal_amygdala_extinction_neuron.new_evidence_summary: McCullough et al. 2016 provides activity-guided RNA-seq markers (Ntsr2/Dkk3/Rspo2/Wnt7a) and Ntsr2 validation for a Thy1-labeled Fear-Off BLA population; Cardenas et al. 2019 supplies the functional/circuit definition (extinction-active, reciprocal mPFC input). Strong molecular + functional support, with a cross-study identity inference linking Fear-Off to extinction neurons.

issues.description: Neurogliaform morphology is asserted by class name and proportion (14-15% of LA/BA GABAergic) rather than a detailed morphological description in the new quote.
No transcriptomic/scRNA-seq marker panel for this class in the new PDF; identity remains marker-based (NPY) and morpho-physiological.
No electrophysiological characterization specific to BLA NPY neurogliaform cells in the new PDF.

bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell.new_evidence_summary: Vereczki et al. 2021 (now an asta_report quote, not just an extraction snippet) anchors the NPY-containing neurogliaform cell as 14-15% of LA/BA GABAergic neurons, with NPY as the defining peptide and GABAergic identity. No ephys or transcriptomic markers added.

issues.description: Evidence is activity-dependent recruitment (orexin-1 antagonism during extinction), not intrinsic membrane/firing properties; supports network recruitment rather than a classical ephys profile.
GABAergic identity supported only at the broader LA/BA interneuron-class level (Vereczki 2021), not for a dedicated calbindin dendrite-targeting cluster.

bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interne.new_evidence_summary: Flores et al. 2017 directly supports calbindin (and not parvalbumin) as a marker and shows activity-dependent recruitment of calbindin+ BLA interneurons during fear extinction, strengthening defining and negative markers and providing an activity-linked ephys handle.

issues.description: All NT support characterizes CeA as a whole (GABAergic / striatum-like), not the large-aspiny subtype specifically. Quotes describe the broader class.
Morphology support is at the CeA-class level (striatum-like medium spiny / GABAergic projection neurons); the large vs small aspiny distinction itself is not resolved by the new quotes.

Hochgerner et al. 2023 (130 neuronal types) and Paul 2025 indicate CeA contains many transcriptomic types; the large-aspiny morphological class is not mapped to a unique gene-defined type, so it may aggregate multiple molecular types.

cea_large_aspiny_neuron.new_evidence_summary: Multiple new reviews (Paul 2025, Chung 2016, Waclaw 2010, Sarowar 2020) plus the Hochgerner 2023 atlas converge on CeA being predominantly GABAergic / striatum-like medium spiny, but none resolves the large-aspiny subtype as a distinct molecular or electrophysiological type; the size/morphology distinction remains unanchored.

issues.description: All NT support characterizes CeA as a whole (GABAergic / striatum-like), not the small-aspiny subtype specifically.
Morphology support is at the CeA-class level; the large vs small aspiny distinction is not resolved by the new quotes.
Hochgerner et al. 2023 (130 neuronal types) and Paul 2025 indicate CeA contains many transcriptomic types; the small-aspiny morphological class is not mapped to a unique gene-defined type.

cea_small_aspiny_neuron.new_evidence_summary: Same converging review/atlas evidence as the large-aspiny node supports CeA GABAergic/striatum-like identity; no new quote distinguishes the small-aspiny subtype molecularly or electrophysiologically.

issues.description: Defined by developmental state (immature excitatory neuron, protracted maturation) rather than a mature somatodendritic morphology.
No mature electrophysiological profile; the quote establishes immature developmental state but not intrinsic membrane properties.
Excitatory (glutamatergic) identity is inferred from 'immature excitatory neurons'; no explicit NT-type assertion in the new quote.
No scRNA-seq or immunohistochemical marker panel supplied for this type in the new PDF.

paralaminar_immature_neuron.new_evidence_summary: Page et al. 2022 establishes the paralaminar nucleus as containing a large population of immature excitatory neurons present at birth (some born from transient local progenitors) that persist with protracted maturation through childhood and adolescence. Developmental-state definition; no molecular markers.
